transcript: I worked in child welfare and so certainly the drug epidemic is something that I have seen for many years as a former caseworker for the Department of Child Services. I also happen to be married to a prosecuting attorney who works a lot in the criminal law. And my community has been hit particularly hard by the opioid epidemic, not just opioids, but other drugs too. And we have seen an emergence of different types of opioid treatment. And Senate Bill 141 came to me from some concerned communities that saw a lot of these types of clinics. They're typically called suboxone clinics that popped up in local communities. Suboxone clinics operate currently in the state of Indiana without very many or any regulations at all. So when this first issue first popped up, there were around 400 suboxone clinics. compared to the 19 or so methadone clinics that we had at that time. I started investigating how they are regulated and found that they're really not regulated at all.
